title: 3D Periodic Table with Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D Periodic Table education scene using Three.js with time control features. Load the GLTFLoader from a CDN.

## Scene Setup
- Set up a Three.js scene with a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 30, 80), looking at origin.
- Use OrbitControls for camera interaction.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.6) and a directional light at (10, 20, 15) with intensity 0.8.
- Background color: #1a1a2e (dark navy).

## Periodic Table Layout
- Create the first 36 elements (H through Kr) of the periodic table as 3D boxes (BoxGeometry 2.8 x 2.8 x 1.0).
- Arrange them in a standard periodic table grid layout. Each cell is spaced 3.2 units apart in X and Z. Row 1 starts at Z=0, Row 2 at Z=-3.2, etc. H is at column 0, He at column 17.
- Color-code elements by category: alkali metals (#ff6b6b), alkaline earth (#ffa06b), transition metals (#6bc5ff), metalloids (#a06bff), nonmetals (#6bff6b), noble gases (#ffff6b), halogens (#ff6bff), other metals (#6bffff).
- Each box should have a TextGeometry or canvas-texture label showing the element symbol and atomic number.
- Store all element meshes in an array.

## Discovery Year Timeline
- Each element has a 'discoveryYear' property. Use approximate real discovery years (e.g., Carbon: -3750, Gold: -6000, Hydrogen: 1766, Helium: 1868, Lithium: 1817, etc.). For ancient elements use negative years.
- Implement a time slider (HTML range input) at the bottom of the screen, ranging from year -8000 to 2020.
- As the slider moves, elements discovered AFTER the selected year should become transparent (opacity 0.15) and sink down (Y = -2), while discovered elements should be fully opaque (opacity 1.0) at Y = 0.
- Animate transitions smoothly using lerp over frames.

## Water Bottle 3D Asset
- Load 'WaterBottle.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place it at position (25, 5, -10) with scale (8, 8, 8).
- This represents a 'chemistry artifact' display. Add a floating label above it: 'H₂O - Water Molecule Demo'.
- When the user clicks on the water bottle, highlight the elements H and O on the periodic table by making them pulse (scale oscillation between 1.0 and 1.4) and change their emissive color to white.
- A second click on the bottle stops the pulsing.

## Time Control Buttons
- Add DOM buttons: 'Play' (auto-advances the timeline slider by 50 years per second), 'Pause', 'Reset' (sets slider to -8000).
- Add a 'Speed' dropdown with options: '1x', '2x', '5x' controlling the playback speed multiplier.
- Display current year prominently as a HUD element: 'Year: {value}'.

## Element Info Panel
- When a user clicks on any element box in the 3D scene, show an info panel (DOM div) on the right side with: Symbol, Name, Atomic Number, Category, Discovery Year.
- Clicking empty space or pressing Escape closes the panel.

## Keyboard Controls
- Press 'T' to toggle between 3D grid layout and a flat table layout (all Y=0, standard 2D periodic table positions).
- Press 'R' to rotate the entire table 360 degrees around Y axis over 3 seconds.
- Press Space to toggle play/pause of timeline.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- currentYear: number (current timeline year from slider)
- visibleElementCount: number (elements with opacity > 0.5)
- totalElements: number (always 36)
- isPlaying: boolean (timeline auto-play state)
- playbackSpeed: number (1, 2, or 5)
- selectedElement: string|null (symbol of clicked element, e.g. 'H', or null)
- infoPanelVisible: boolean
- layoutMode: '3d'|'flat'
- isRotating: boolean
- waterBottleLoaded: boolean
- waterBottleHighlightActive: boolean
- hydrogenHighlighted: boolean
- oxygenHighlighted: boolean
- elementPositions: object mapping symbol to {x,y,z}
- cameraPosition: {x,y,z}

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Elements must smoothly interpolate position and opacity when timeline changes. No NaN values in any positions. Element Y positions must be either 0 (visible) or -2 (hidden) at steady state. Pulsing scale must stay within [1.0, 1.4]. Camera must remain within reasonable bounds.
